reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
September 1st has always felt like a soft reset to me. Summer's loud season is fading, school buses are back on the roads, and there's a particular quality of light in the evening that says: something is turning over. You don't need a New Year to start again. Any Tuesday will do.

When I was drinking, I collected first days like receipts. Monday was going to be different. This month was going to be different. After this trip, after this breakup, after this bender. The plan was always the plan. The life was always the drinking. What I didn't understand yet was that a life doesn't get built in the grand gesture. It gets built in what you do at 7am when nobody's watching, and what you do at 9pm when the day was hard and the old voice gets loud. Aristotle nailed it two thousand years ago and Durant said it cleaner: you are what you keep doing.

So here's the small, unglamorous truth of eleven years in — the days that changed my life didn't feel like they were changing my life. They felt like Tuesdays. Coffee, a walk, a phone call I didn't want to make, going to bed sober again. Stack enough of those and one day you look up and you're skiing in Whistler, or standing in a field at dawn with your rifle and your dog, thinking: I get to be here for this. That's the whole thing.
reflection.meditation: What is one small, unglamorous action I can repeat today that the future me will thank me for?

affirmations: I am building my life in the quiet hours, not the loud ones.
Today I choose the action, not the mood.
I am someone who shows up — for myself first, and everyone else after.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for the boring miracle of another sober Tuesday. Grateful for morning coffee that actually tastes like something, for a body that remembers last night clearly, and for the fact that I get to start again without having to apologize first. There was a version of me who couldn't imagine wanting a day like this. He'd be stunned at what ordinary feels like now.
gratitude.closing: One day. This one. That's the work.
